A 48-year-old male with pancreatic cancer is admitted to the surgical ICU after undergoing a
pancreaticoduodenectomy. His daily drainage output has exceeded 1 liter for three consecutive days.
On the fourth postoperative day, nursing staff reports decreased responsiveness. His vital signs show:
- Temperature: 99.5°F (37.5°C) - Blood pressure: 107/88 mmHg - Heart rate: 120/min - Respiratory
rate: 17/min - O2 saturation: 98% on room air Physical examination reveals dry skin and mucous
membranes. Laboratory results show: Serum values: - Na+: 154 mEq/L - Cl-: 100 mEq/L - K+: 4.3
mEq/L - HCO3-: 27 mEq/L - BUN: 20 mg/dL - Glucose: 99 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL What is the
most appropriate immediate management step? Answer Choices: (A) 3% saline IV (B) Free water
replacement IV (C) 0.45% saline IV (D) Oral rehydration therapy (E) Sodium bicarbonate IV (F)
Vasopressors (G) 0.9% saline IV (H) Continuous infusion of furosemide (I) 5% dextrose IV (J) Lactated
Ringer's solution IV
 A. Free water replacement IV
B. 3% saline IV
C. Lactated Ringer's solution IV
D. 0.9% saline IV
E. Continuous infusion of furosemide
F. Oral rehydration therapy
G. Sodium bicarbonate IV
H. 0.45% saline IV
I. Vasopressors
J. 5% dextrose IV
